jobs.description:
Dallas is Growing. Grow With Us.

Looking for more than just a job? The City of Dallas offers careers with purpose. With competitive benefits, growth opportunities, and a vibrant work culture,

we’re committed to helping you thrive while you help our city flourish. Be part of a team that’s committed to service, innovation, and community.

Job Summary

Job Description

Overview

The Superintendent - Environmental Quality administers, oversees, manages, and monitors all operation activities in Pretreatment, Industrial Monitoring, Liquid Waste, and Special Projects & Outreach or Laboratory within the Pretreatment and Laboratory Services (PALS) Division of the Dallas Water Utilities, or/and oversees Park Conservation and Natural Resources, manages and oversees wildlife habitat efforts, manages Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program and staff, coordinates interdepartmental conservation efforts.

Essential Functions

Manages, directs, and leads all operations and activities of the Pretreatment or Laboratory operations or various departmental initiatives regarding Habitat Management, Natural Resource Conservation, or/and environmental strategic planning through supervisors for compliance with TCEQ's Pretreatment permit and other Federal and State regulatory requirements; ensures that all acceptable operating procedures are followed and that operations are efficient and follow regulatory requirements.
Prepares and presents clear, complete, and concise correspondence and technical reports; coordinates and collaborates with other City departments; interacts, engages, and communicates with TCEQ and EPA regarding current regulations, permit compliance, and other matters regarding wastewater operations or/and wildlife conservation, natural resource conservation, pest management.
Manages the hiring and performance evaluation procedures for the department; approves and enforces discipline, verifies and approves time, manages service contracts, equipment, and technology and facilitates departmental success and adherence to permitting and regulatory standards; hears and resolves grievances and implements disciplinary actions when necessary.
Develops and implements long range plans, programs, and schedules to ensure operational efficiency and compliance; determines goals and objectives needing emphasis; directs and coordinates work through supervisors, staff or/and volunteer groups, and provides coaching, advice, counsel, or technical direction as needed; prioritizes tasks, schedules and assigns various requests, and administers City policies and procedures.
Responds to, engages with, and oversees the handling of customer requests and inquiries; acts as a liaison with TCEQ, EPA, and other organizations to improve customer service and regulatory compliance while ensuring safety and City standards.
Supervises the preparation of Pretreatment or Laboratory or/and other reports and documents; coordinates and facilitates the provision of Pretreatment or Laboratory supplies, or/and equipment maintenance contracts, or/and the oversight of maintenance agreements for Pretreatment or Laboratory software and systems; or/and prepares the Annual Pretreatment or Laboratory Report, and oversees the compliance of other regulatory reporting.
Develops and implements budget for department and operations; inspects work, audits activities, and identifies equipment that needs to be procured; attends meetings with upper management regarding operating budget preparation and approval.
Coaches, advises, counsels and instructs employees; identifies all training needs for employees; interviews and makes selection on candidates for filling positions, recommends terminations, and facilitates promotions; hears and resolves serious complaints or simple grievances from employees and refers serious grievances to higher level managers.
Finds and implements methods to improve production or effectiveness; oversees the inspection of pretreatment or laboratory procedures, or/and maintenance activities, and project implementation; approves employee hours and ensures adherence to all personnel and departmental policies and procedures.
Performs any and all other work as needed or assigned.

Knowledge And Skills

Knowledge of departmental management.
Knowledge of Water and Wastewater systems and general equipment, facilities, and plant maintenance or/and Natural Resources/Parks Conservation, Wildlife Habitat Management.
Knowledge of inspection procedures and environmental compliance standards.
Knowledge of local, state, and federal regulations relevant to the operations of the Pretreatment program standards or/and Pesticide Management, Forestry/Natural Resources Management and other regulatory requirements
Ability to prioritize work, provide training, and facilitate efficient service delivery.
Ability to follow and give oral and written instructions and read charts and maintain written records.
Ability to participate in budget development, procurement activities, and inventory management.
Ability to maintain record keeping or work log system.
Communicating effectively verbally and in writing.
Knowledge of Federal, State, local standards that affect park activities.
Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships.

Education

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in a Biology, Chemistry, Engineering or Environmental Science field.

Experience

Five (5) years of experience in environmental/industrial waste control, laboratory operations/management, basic chemical analysis, water/soil/air quality sample collection or wastewater collection/pretreatment discharge monitoring.

AND

Two (2) years of supervisory/management involved working with federal and state environmental regulatory agencies (Environmental Protection Agency-EPA, Texas Commission on Environmental Quality-TCEQ) (This experience may be included in the required experience listed above.)

Equivalency(ies)

An associate degree in any field plus seven (7) years of the required experience including two (2) years of the stated supervisory/project management experience will meet the education and experience requirements.
A bachelor's degree or higher in a non-specified field plus seven (7) years of the required experience including two (2) years of the stated supervisory/project management experience will meet the education and experience requirements.
A master's degree or higher in a specified field plus three (3) years of the required experience including two (2) years of the stated supervisory/project management experience will meet the education and experience requirements.

Job Description Summary

Job Description

The Project Data Coordinator supports the ADRD Public Health Adoption Accelerator's research infrastructure by managing all data collection, entry, extraction, quality assurance, and reporting functions. Reporting to the Project Director with scientific oversight from Dr. Glanz (Strategy 1 lead), the Coordinator executes the annual environmental scan of BOLD program implementation strategies, manages the Penn REDCap database for performance measures and TA engagement logs, and compiles quantitative data for CDC Annual Performance Reports. This position is the operational hub for the program's evidence base.

Job Responsibilities

Execute and manage the annual environmental scan of BOLD program implementation strategies across ≥30 STLT agencies, Component 1 and 2 activities, peer-reviewed literature and grey literature using the dual-review structured extraction protocol developed with Drs. Glanz and Gitlin; train and supervise Penn RAs in extraction coding procedures.
Build, maintain, and update the Penn REDCap database for all program data streams, including quarterly performance measures (tools/trainings used nationally and by STLT agencies; communications products shared), TA engagement logs, adoption-tier classifications, FRAME-IS adaptation notes, and Launch pad site implementation outcome data using the Proctor et al. framework.
Compile and prepare all quantitative performance measure data for CDC quarterly reporting and Annual Performance Reports; coordinate with Emory external evaluation team on data verification procedures; generate equity-disaggregated reach tracking reports from Year 1.
Manage content entry and annual updates for the Implementation Strategy Registry; coordinate with Dr. Demiris on Registry digital infrastructure; perform quality review of Registry entries for accuracy and completeness against CPSTFCPSTF-modeled rating criteria.
Provide data management support for Launchpad sites in coordination with Gaugler lab RA; conduct data audits, generate site-level reports, and flag data quality issues to Dr. Hirschman and the Project Director.
Provide administrative and logistical support for the annual Expert Advisory Panel convening and Evidence Academy, including materials preparation, rating instrument management, and meeting documentation.
Other responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 1 to 2 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience is required. Master's degree preferred. Fields of study: public health, health sciences, information science, or related discipline.
1–3 years of experience in data management, research coordination, or program evaluation. Experience with REDCap, Qualtrics, or equivalent data entry and management systems required. Experience with grant reporting preferred.
Required Skills: REDCap, Microsoft Excel (data entry, extraction, and auditing); quantitative research methods; attention to detail; time management; written communication. Familiarity with ADRD, aging, or public health research preferred.

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Who are we looking for?

We’re looking for an Environmental Human Health / Ecological Risk Assessor
to join our team! In this role, you’ll lead and perform human health and ecological risk assessments under a variety of North American and international regulatory frameworks, addressing both traditional and emerging contaminants like PFAS. You will also contribute to Natural Resource Damage Assessments (NRDAs), develop work plans, and oversee field investigations that support ERA, HHRA, and NRDA efforts. Your expertise will support emergency response initiatives related to chemical fate, transport, and toxicology. You will collaborate across GHD’s global network, engage directly with clients and regulatory agencies, and represent the team in technical and trade organizations, while also mentoring and coaching young professionals and colleagues.

At GHD, our Risk Assessors are engaged in projects that apply risk assessment and risk management strategies to support contaminated site decision-making under Federal, state, and international site cleanup programs. This includes supporting and implementing site characterization and remedial action projects that involve efforts to identify and control potentially unacceptable human and ecological exposures to chemicals in the environment.

This position can be based in Syracuse, NY
, King of Prussia, PA
, or Little Rock, AR
.

Our Hybrid Work Model:

Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Data Analysis: Conduct research using primary data sources, and select information needed for the analysis of key themes and trends.
Personal Capability Building: Develop own capabilities by participating in assessment and development planning activities as well as formal and informal training and coaching; gain or maintain external professional accreditation, where relevant, to improve performance and fulfill personal potential. Maintain an in-depth understanding of technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Client & Customer Management: Manage important client relationships with guidance from senior colleagues, or oversee relationship management with a group of more transactional clients and customers.
Solutions Analysis: Analyze specific problems and issues to find the best solutions.
Insights and Reporting: Prepare and coordinate the completion of various data and analytics reports.

What you will bring to the team:

Master’s or PhD in Biology, Ecology, Ecotoxicology, Toxicology, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or related technical field
7-12 years of experience with Ecological and Human Health Risk Assessment and/or Natural Resource Damage Assessment
Excellent quantitative skill and experience in data analysis, biostatistics, etc.
Excellent oral and written communication skills to tell the story of the assessment
Willingness to travel throughout North America
Experience working directly with industrial clients

Take on some of the world’s toughest challenges - with GHD supporting you every step of the way.

We'll give you control over your career, empower you to find innovative solutions and help you create a lasting impact.

See where your commitment could take you with GHD.

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding a remote Senior Environmental Compliance Manager to our NEPA team based in San Antonio, TX .

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Your Impact

We are seeking a Senior Environmental Compliance Manager to lead complex environmental compliance, permitting, and National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) efforts for federal, state, local, and private-sector clients. This remote senior role combines environmental policy and regulatory expertise with strong technical writing, project management, agency coordination, permitting, stakeholder engagement, and quality oversight. The successful candidate will lead multidisciplinary teams through environmental review and permitting processes, translate complex regulatory and technical requirements into clear and defensible documentation, and help clients manage environmental commitments and compliance risk throughout project planning, permitting, construction, and implementation.

Responsibilities

Lead preparation, review, and delivery of NEPA documents, including Environmental Impact Statements (EIS), Environmental Assessments (EA), Categorical Exclusion (CatEx) documentation, and supporting technical analyses.
Lead and coordinate environmental compliance under applicable federal and state requirements, including the Endangered Species Act (ESA), Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act/Essential Fish Habitat (EFH), National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) Section 106, and other resource-specific statutes and regulations.
Lead federal and state permitting and consultation efforts, including pre-application strategy, application development, agency coordination, consultation schedules, permit conditions, and documentation of compliance milestones.
Manage complex environmental projects and multidisciplinary teams, including subject matter experts, technical authors, subcontractors, and project support staff; establish priorities and maintain alignment with scope, schedule, budget, and client expectations.
Develop environmental compliance strategies for complex or environmentally sensitive projects and identify practical approaches to regulatory, permitting, mitigation, and implementation challenges.
Interpret statutes, regulations, agency guidance, permit conditions, and policy requirements; evaluate how changes in project design or implementation may affect environmental approvals and compliance obligations.
Prepare, review, and edit technical and regulatory documents for accuracy, consistency, defensibility, readability, and compliance with client and agency requirements.
Develop and manage permit and environmental commitment matrices, registers, databases, and other tracking systems to support implementation, monitoring, reporting, and agency submissions.
Coordinate with federal, state, and local agencies and facilitate interagency consultation and communication on complex environmental issues.
Plan and support public and stakeholder engagement, including scoping, public meetings, stakeholder communications, outreach materials, comment tracking, and response development.
Communicate complex scientific, technical, regulatory, and policy information clearly to clients, agencies, stakeholders, project teams, and the public.
Support environmental compliance and permitting for infrastructure, water resources, coastal and marine, energy, transportation, military/DoD, and other federal or major development projects, as applicable.
Provide senior-level quality assurance/quality control and technical review of environmental documents, permit applications, consultation packages, compliance plans, and client deliverables.
Support client relationship management, proposal development, scopes of work, level-of-effort estimates, and identification of follow-on environmental compliance and permitting needs.
Mentor and provide technical guidance to environmental planners, specialists, and project staff.
Other duties as assigned.

Conduct activities in line with internal procedures, legislation, and industry standards.

Pursue continuous professional development and maintain a high degree of discipline, knowledge and awareness.
Work in a safe manner at all times and report all health and safety incidents and concerns.
Additional duties as required.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental policy, natural resources, planning, biology, marine science, engineering, or a related field; advanced education or substantial directly relevant experience may be considered as part of the overall qualifications.

15+ years of progressively responsible experience in environmental compliance, NEPA, permitting, environmental policy, natural resource management, or a closely related field, including experience serving in a senior technical, project management, permitting, or environmental compliance role.
Demonstrated experience leading and managing complex environmental compliance, NEPA, permitting, and/or consultation efforts, including multidisciplinary teams, schedules, budgets, deliverables, and client or agency coordination.
Strong working knowledge of NEPA and experience preparing and/or reviewing EISs, EAs, Categorical Exclusion documentation, and other environmental review documents.
Experience interpreting and applying federal environmental regulatory and policy requirements, including consultation and permitting processes such as ESA Section 7, EFH, NHPA Section 106, and other applicable natural resource compliance requirements.
Experience developing, implementing, and tracking environmental commitments, permit conditions, compliance plans, commitment registers, databases, or similar compliance management tools.
Excellent technical writing, editing, analytical, communication, facilitation, and organizational skills, with the ability to synthesize complex technical, scientific, regulatory, and policy information for technical and nontechnical audiences.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across disciplines, agencies, clients, and stakeholder groups, including experience with public involvement, interagency coordination, and complex or potentially contentious environmental issues.
Experience supporting federal agencies and complex projects involving areas such as coastal and marine resources, water resources, offshore energy, restoration, infrastructure, military, or transportation is preferred; experience developing environmental policy, regulatory procedures, guidance, or rulemaking documents is also desirable. Periodic travel may be required.

This position requires the candidate to be a U.S. Citizen due to the projects they will be working on.

Auckland Zoo is a conservation and community-serving cultural organisation with a mission to bring people together to build a future for wildlife. Through science, learning and engagement, and strengthening our relationship with Te Ao Māori, we strive for excellence in animal care and welfare, conserve wildlife in the wild, and nurture a lifelong connection with nature to enhance the wellbeing of our communities.

We are looking for a Conservation Learning Facilitator - Online Learning to join our Conservation Advocacy and Engagement department.

This exciting role combines developing and delivering Auckland Zoo's conservation learning programmes with specialist responsibility for our growing online learning portfolio. We are seeking an experienced educator with demonstrated skills and experience in online learning design, digital content development and Learning Management System (LMS) administration. Working within the Conservation Learning and Community Engagement team, you will coordinate the development and continuous improvement of our Conservation Learning Online programmes while also delivering impactful learning experiences to schools and other audiences both in-person and online

The successful candidate will help expand the reach and impact of Auckland Zoo's conservation learning programmes by combining strong educational practice with innovative digital learning approaches.

The key deliverables for the successful candidate will be to:

Develop, deliver and evaluate high-quality conservation learning programmes for schools and other audiences onsite, offsite and online.
Create learning experiences that align with the New Zealand Curriculum, Ministry of Education guidance, Auckland Zoo's mission and conservation outcomes.
Act as the Conservation Learning and Community Engagement team's specialist for online learning, leading the development, administration and continuous improvement of Auckland Zoo's online learning programmes and Learning Management System.
Develop and maintain engaging online courses, learning resources and digital content that support conservation outcomes and learner engagement.
Monitor learner participation, platform performance and programme outcomes, using data and feedback to inform improvements and growth.
Support colleagues across Auckland Zoo to utilise the Learning Management System for learning, training and development purposes.
Contribute to the expansion, reach and impact of Conservation Learning Online and wider conservation learning programmes.
Collaborate with colleagues across Conservation Advocacy and Engagement, the wider Zoo and external education partners to achieve shared conservation and learning goals.

Experience developing, delivering and evaluating educational or conservation learning programmes.

Experience with Moodle or another Learning Management System, or the ability to quickly learn new systems.
Knowledge of the New Zealand Curriculum and effective learning and engagement practices.
Excellent communication, organisational and project management skills.
A strong commitment to conservation and a desire to inspire action for wildlife and wild places.

jobs.description:
Performance Drone Works (PDW) is building the next generation of tactical robotic systems used across defense, national security, and public safety missions. We are building a new center of engineering excellence to design our new category of tactical robotic systems and the industrial capacity to deliver them, bringing decisive airpower into the hands of every operator. We are not here to make promises; we are here to deliver real systems with real capabilities for real missions. 

You will join a team of operators, engineers, and builders who solve hard problems with humility and focus. We design and produce multi-mission aerial systems that operators trust to perform in real-world conditions, reliably, repeatedly, and at scale. Our approach is grounded in operator-centered design, rapid iteration from field use, and U.S.-based manufacturing. We operate by a clear set of values: Mission First, Aim Farther, Own It, Win Together. This is how we build advantage and how we help protect our service members, our communities, and our country. 

What

You’ll

Do

Conduct flight operations for PDW sUAS in support of test, evaluation, and development activities.
Execute flight acceptance tests for production aircraft and associated equipment to verify system performance, quality, and readiness.
Perform regression testing of hardware, software and configuration changes to confirm expected aircraft behavior.
Support testing of new features, payload integrations, and emerging capabilities through structured flight test events.
Fly prototype and early-development aircraft to help engineering evaluate new designs, controls, and system behavior.
Develop deep technical understanding of PDW aircraft, payloads, subsystems, and normal flight characteristics to serve as a system expert to identify system anomalies that may not be immediately apparent during typical operations.
Document flight results, discrepancies, failures, and observed issues in a clear, complete, and actionable manner.
Conduct flight demonstrations for PDW customers.
Strictly follow all flight safety procedures, range/test site protocols, and operational risk controls during ground and flight operations.
Make sound go/no-go and in-flight risk decisions to protect personnel, equipment, test assets, and company interests.

Requirements

3+ years of experience in operating and maintaining sUAS systems.
Associate’s in engineering, Engineering Technology or equivalent work experience in a related field.
Ability to read and interpret technical documentation including, in-depth test plans and assembly instructions.
Experience supporting flight test, developmental test, or validation activities for new unmanned aircraft systems or payloads.
Familiarity with logging tools, test documentation systems, issue tracking, or basic troubleshooting workflows in an engineering environment.
Ability to read and interpret technical documentation including, in-depth test plans.
Has or in process of obtaining FAA Part 107 certification.
Excellent written and oral communications skills.
Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Ability to sit, stand, bend, reach, climb, and move about regularly throughout the day and lift / carry up to 50 pounds. Must have manual dexterity to operate standard office equipment as well as remote control systems, ground support equipment, and sUAS hardware. Must be physically capable of conducting field-based flight operations, setting up flight equipment in various terrains, handling and assembling sUAS components, and operating in outdoor conditions for extended periods.

Work Environment

This position operates in a combination of standard office, lab, and outdoor field environments. This role requires use of standard office equipment and involves regular exposure to drone systems, ground control stations, diagnostic tools, and potentially hazardous materials such as lithium polymer batteries. The position requires frequent travel to flight test sites, customer locations, and supplier facilities. Work may be conducted in outdoor environments under varying weather conditions and non-climate-controlled settings, and may include exposure to noise, dust, and uneven terrain. Personal protective equipment (PPE) may be required depending on the testing environment. This is a fast-paced work environment requiring cross-functional collaboration, self-direction, and team-based responsibilities. Standard work hours for this position are Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, with occasional evenings, weekends, and travel required based on operational demands.

Benefits  

PDW values our team, and we offer a compensation package reflective of your experience and capabilities. Benefits include:  

Comprehensive BCBS medical, dental, and vision coverage; 80% sponsored by the company.  
Safe Harbor 401(K) with company match.  
Paid Parental Leave.  
On-site gym at Huntsville, AL & Denver, CO locations.
Employer provided life insurance.  
Robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP).  
A work environment that encourages teamwork and innovation.  
Competitive salary, generous paid time off (PTO), and flexible leave options.

Founded to help bridge the gap between policy and practice, our mission is to enable people and the planet to meet the pace of change by expanding access to new technologies that power more sustainable and equitable outcomes.

By embracing whole-system thinking and state-of-the-art technology, we enable partners across public, private, and nonprofit sectors to tackle complex, real-world challenges—like housing affordability, ecosystem conservation, water management, and sustainable infrastructure—with greater clarity.

Our work liberates and connects key information, creates nuanced pictures of complex situations, and makes land, water, and social data easier to use, understand, and act on. We use tools like satellite data and artificial intelligence to deliver insights for impact.

jobs.description:
PRIMARY PURPOSE
  
This position is located in Houston, TX.
  
CNA’s Center for Homeland Security and Infrastructure Resilience develops data-driven, analytic solutions to address complex and emerging problems. We conduct analysis and planning, build decision-support tools, and create training and exercises that support the safety and security of our nation’s residents, visitors, environment, infrastructure, economy and cyberspace.
  
We are hiring for a Research Specialist to work out of Houston, TX (relocation is not allocated for this role). This is a hybrid role that would consist of remote work and travelling to client sites.
  
Staff at this level would support project and other corporate needs including through (1) collecting, processing, vetting, and analyzing pertinent data, especially geospatial data, for further use and/or (2) conducting technical assistance activities such as planning and organizing meetings and seminars, and/or (3) supporting the process of developing and submitting proposals through collecting and organizing resumes, past performance reports, and corporate capabilities.
  
CNA fosters an inclusive culture that values diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Our flexible and engaging work environment encourages iterative and creative collaboration at every stage of the problem-solving process. Our employees are committed to helping clients develop effective solutions to better manage their programs through scientific, data-driven approaches. We are looking for creative and innovative individuals to help carry out our mission.
  
  
JOB DESCRIPTION AND/OR DUTIES
  
1. Apply standard research methodologies to gather, process, and analyze data. Use relevant database software to effectively organize and present data and generate reports. Demonstrate facility at the intermediate level with Microsoft Office and other standard CNA software packages to accomplish primary duties.
  
  
2. Develop a basic familiarity with the missions and organizational structure of the division or team's major client/sponsors.
  
  
3. Participate in meetings with project team. Support preparation for client/sponsor interactions. Identify client/sponsor POC for their projects.
  
  
4. Develop a sufficient understanding or expertise on specific tasks, issues or data so as to make a positive contribution to project outcomes.
  
  
5. Develop basic knowledge about CNA, its organization, key personnel and personalities, and relevant CNA standard operating procedures (SOPs), to include basic knowledge of CNA business environment. Understand the concepts of core, above core, and above ceiling/ domestic. Have basic awareness of the project development process.
  
  
6. Possess the skills necessary to communicate information concisely, precisely, and in a grammatically correct manner in oral and written communication. Present and summarize data effectively.
  
  
7. Work under close supervision on focused, well-structured pieces of projects. Tracks personal project spending.
  
  
8. Exhibit a positive attitude in interactions with colleagues, clients/sponsors, and staff. Take initiative offering assistance when opportunities arise.
  
  
9. Perform other duties as assigned.
  
  
JOB REQUIREMENTS
  
**1. Education:** Bachelor’s degree in related field or equivalent experience required.
  
**2. Experience:** Strong preference will be given to candidates that have experience with the following:
  

* Professional work experience, ideally in support of a government agency and ideally applying geospatial analysis
* Geospatial analysis software, especially ArcGIS Online (AGOL), as well as ArcPro and the entire suite of Esri products for mapping, data visualization, and analysis. Demonstrate proficiency with Esri’s Arc GIS Online (AGOL), including the software’s functionality and organization administration.
* Statistical analysis and use of interactive dashboarding tools such as Power BI
* Experience working in Python or R
* Ability to work independently on discrete tasks

**3. Skills:**  

* Computer skills; Microsoft Office; database management
* Coding, analysis, and dashboarding
* Very good interpersonal and oral and written communication skills
* Training and presenting

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
Description

"

As a GIS Analyst with AMS, your office is wherever data meets the real world. Whether mapping utility corridors in urban centers or analyzing terrain in remote forests, you play a critical role in supporting safe and efficient utility operations. As an AMS GIS Analyst, you will transform spatial data into actionable insights that help keep the lights on and communities safe.

Some of the most important characteristics of an AMS GIS Analyst are attention to detail, analytical thinking, and the ability to communicate complex spatial information clearly. You are accountable for advancing a culture of safety and excellence while providing quality and value to our customers and clients.

The pay range for this position is from $20.00 to $30.00 per hour, contingent upon relevant education, experience, and industry-specific certifications. This specified range is determined by the tier associated with the job posting. However, should the employee be classified under a different tier, the compensation may fall outside the stated range.

WHAT WE OFFER:

Industry competitive pay
Medical/Health/Dental/Vision/VOYA/Paid Holidays/EAP eligibility on day one of employment (Full-Time Employees)
401K, Vacation Accrual, life insurance, long-term disability eligibility first of the month after 3 months of service
Sick Time eligibility on day 90 of employment
Weekly paychecks and direct deposit
Participation in the Employee Referral Program (must meet eligibility requirements)
Boot and clothing program (company funded, if applicable)
Ongoing training and assistance with obtaining industry certifications

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Analyze and interpret spatial data to support utility vegetation management (UVM) programs and infrastructure planning
Create, maintain, and update GIS databases, maps, and dashboards
Perform spatial analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities
Respond to data inquiries & support field crews and arborists with reports, maps, spreadsheets, etc.
Manage specialized databases and spreadsheets, entering data and generating reports with proficiency in Microsoft Excel
Collaborate with field teams to integrate GPS-collected data into GIS systems
Generate reports and visualizations to support decision-making and regulatory compliance
Ensure data accuracy and consistency across platforms and projects
Support QA/QC processes for spatial data and field-collected information
Assist in developing and maintaining automated workflows using GIS tools and scripting
Travel may be required for field data collection or coordination with field teams

WHAT YOU NEED TO HAVE:

1-2 years of experience working with GIS software and databases, including ESRI Suite
Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or a related field
Proficiency in GIS software (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS)
Experience with spatial data formats and coordinate systems
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to work independently,manage multiple tasks, and show attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Basic programming/scripting knowledge (e.g., Python, SQL) is a plus
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel if needed

WHAT WOULD BE AMAZING TO HAVE:

Experience in utility or environmental GIS applications
Familiarity with GPS data collection tools and mobile GIS apps
Certification such as GISP or Esri Technical Certification
UVM Experience
Bi-Lingual (English/Spanish) a plus

Working Environment

Primarily office-based with occasional fieldwork; may involve travel to utility corridors or remote locations. Work may include exposure to various weather conditions and terrain. Reasonable accommodation, if available, may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.

Physical

Must be able to sit or stand for extended periods, operate a computer and related equipment, and occasionally travel to field sites. Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. and walk on uneven terrain may be required for field data collection.

Company Overview

Arbormetrics (AMS) is a leading provider of vegetation and asset management consulting services to the utility industry. Successful professionals at AMS have come from a variety of backgrounds, including: GIS, geography, environmental science, forestry, natural resource management, and more. For more information visit our website www.arbormetrics.com

Applicants must pass a pre-employment drug test and a criminal background check.

All candidates must possess a valid driver's license and have a good driving record.

AMS is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. EOE/AA : Minority/Female/ Vets/ Disabled.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Are you ready to shape the future technological landscape in Europe?

We are dedicated to responsible digitalisation, building innovative, inclusive solutions that drive meaningful impact. With over 8,900 professionals across Europe, we help EU institutions, public and private organisations thrive in a rapidly evolving digital world. Are you ready to shape the future through technology? Your journey starts here. Take a look at some of our impactful projects here: https://netcompany.com/cases/

Job Description

The Senior Geospatial Data & GIS Scientist provides expertise in geospatial technologies, spatial data management, cloud-based GIS solutions, and geospatial analytics. The role supports the design, implementation, integration, and optimization of geospatial data platforms and services while ensuring data quality, interoperability, governance, and compliance with relevant standards.

What Would Make You a Fit For The Role

Design, develop, and maintain geospatial solutions using GIS platforms, spatial databases, and open-source geospatial technologies.
Perform geospatial data processing, analysis, transformation, and automation using Python and spatial analytics tools.
Develop and optimize spatial databases, data models, and geospatial data integration workflows.
Implement and support cloud-based geospatial processing and analytics solutions in Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud environments.
Contribute to the integration of geospatial data within data lake, lakehouse, and enterprise analytics architectures.
Ensure adherence to metadata standards, interoperability requirements, data governance principles, and open data best practices.
Assess technical feasibility, risks, dependencies, and solution options, providing recommendations to stakeholders and project teams.
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and communicate technical concepts, findings, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Qualifications

What would make you a fit for the role:

Bachelor's degree in Geography, GIS, Geoinformatics, Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Proven experience with GIS desktop, server, and open-source geospatial technologies such as ArcGIS, QGIS, PostGIS, GeoServer, GDAL/OGR, or equivalent.
Strong Python programming skills for geospatial processing using libraries such as GeoPandas, Rasterio, Shapely, Fiona, PyProj, Xarray, or similar.
Experience with SQL and spatial SQL, including spatial database technologies such as PostGIS, SQL Server Spatial, or equivalent.
Hands-on experience with cloud-based geospatial processing and analytics solutions in Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud environments.
Knowledge of data lake/lakehouse architectures, geospatial data integration, metadata standards (ISO 19115, DCAT/DCAT-AP, Dublin Core), and interoperability principles.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to data quality, reproducibility, documentation, and operational maintainability.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills in English
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary environments
Understanding of SDMX, environmental indicators, or statistical-geospatial integration is considered an asset.

Additional Information

If you are looking forward to be part of a diverse environment, and have the opportunity to work alongside well-experienced professionals, on challenging, large-scale projects that directly impact millions of citizens around the globe, then this is the place to be!

Description

"

As a GIS Analyst with AMS, your office is wherever data meets the real world. Whether mapping utility corridors in urban centers or analyzing terrain in remote forests, you play a critical role in supporting safe and efficient utility operations. As an AMS GIS Analyst, you will transform spatial data into actionable insights that help keep the lights on and communities safe.

Some of the most important characteristics of an AMS GIS Analyst are attention to detail, analytical thinking, and the ability to communicate complex spatial information clearly. You are accountable for advancing a culture of safety and excellence while providing quality and value to our customers and clients.

The pay range for this position is from $20.00 to $30.00 per hour, contingent upon relevant education, experience, and industry-specific certifications. This specified range is determined by the tier associated with the job posting. However, should the employee be classified under a different tier, the compensation may fall outside the stated range.

WHAT WE OFFER:

Industry competitive pay
Medical/Health/Dental/Vision/VOYA/Paid Holidays/EAP eligibility on day one of employment (Full-Time Employees)
401K, Vacation Accrual, life insurance, long-term disability eligibility first of the month after 3 months of service
Sick Time eligibility on day 90 of employment
Weekly paychecks and direct deposit
Participation in the Employee Referral Program (must meet eligibility requirements)
Boot and clothing program (company funded, if applicable)
Ongoing training and assistance with obtaining industry certifications

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Analyze and interpret spatial data to support utility vegetation management (UVM) programs and infrastructure planning
Create, maintain, and update GIS databases, maps, and dashboards
Perform spatial analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities
Respond to data inquiries & support field crews and arborists with reports, maps, spreadsheets, etc.
Manage specialized databases and spreadsheets, entering data and generating reports with proficiency in Microsoft Excel
Collaborate with field teams to integrate GPS-collected data into GIS systems
Generate reports and visualizations to support decision-making and regulatory compliance
Ensure data accuracy and consistency across platforms and projects
Support QA/QC processes for spatial data and field-collected information
Assist in developing and maintaining automated workflows using GIS tools and scripting
Travel may be required for field data collection or coordination with field teams

1-2 years of experience working with GIS software and databases, including ESRI Suite
Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or a related field

Experience with spatial data formats and coordinate systems
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to work independently,manage multiple tasks, and show attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Basic programming/scripting knowledge (e.g., Python, SQL) is a plus
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel if needed

WHAT WOULD BE AMAZING TO HAVE:

Experience in utility or environmental GIS applications
Familiarity with GPS data collection tools and mobile GIS apps
Certification such as GISP or Esri Technical Certification
UVM Experience
Bi-Lingual (English/Spanish) a plus

Working Environment

Primarily office-based with occasional fieldwork; may involve travel to utility corridors or remote locations. Work may include exposure to various weather conditions and terrain. Must be able to sit or stand for extended periods, operate a computer and related equipment, and occasionally travel to field sites. Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. and walk on uneven terrain may be required for field data collection.

Et si votre prochain défi consistait à savoir précisément où l’on se trouve… là où le GPS ne suffit plus ?

SBG Systems conçoit et fabrique en France des technologies de navigation inertielle de haute précision, utilisées partout dans le monde.

Nos systèmes combinent capteurs MEMS de pointe, GNSS et algorithmes avancés de fusion de données pour permettre à des équipements autonomes de se localiser, de s’orienter et de naviguer avec une extrême précision. Drones, robots terrestres, navires océanographiques, aéronautique, spatial ou défense : nos technologies opèrent là où les environnements sont hostiles et où la précision ne tolère aucune approximation.

Entreprise française indépendante, nous faisons le choix fort de maîtriser nos produits de bout en bout : de la recherche fondamentale et la R&D logicielle/matérielle jusqu'à la production industrielle sur notre site. Présents aujourd'hui dans plus de 70 pays, nous équipons les acteurs technologiques et industriels les plus exigeants de la planète.

Aujourd’hui en hypercroissance, SBG Systems change d’échelle avec un défi majeur : grandir vite sans jamais transiger sur l’excellence technologique, l'agilité et l'esprit d'équipe qui font notre différence.

Ce passage à l'échelle se joue au plus près du terrain : pour notre équipe Field Application, cela implique d'accompagner des programmes d’intégration de plus en plus critiques et de bâtir l'expertise de pointe nécessaire pour sécuriser les missions de nos clients.

C’est au cœur de cette dynamique que nous renforçons notre pôle d'expertise technique dédié aux applications Défense et Systèmes Autonomes (UAV).

Votre rôle : L'expertise technique au service du terrain et du produit

Intégré(e) Au Sein D’une Équipe De 10 Personnes Rattachée à Christophe, Directeur Support Client, Vous Rejoignez Le Pôle D'excellence Niveau 3 Aux Côtés D'un Autre Expert Senior Chevronné. Vous Devenez Le Référent Applicatif Dédié Aux Intégrations Complexes Sur Vecteurs Aériens Et Systèmes Militaires Non Habités

Expertise client & Intégration avancée (N3) : Conseiller et auditer les grands intégrateurs et constructeurs de drones de défense dans le choix, l’interfaçage et l’optimisation de leurs architectures de navigation.
Intégration Autopilote & Navigation : Résoudre les problématiques complexes de couplage GNSS/Inertiel avec les couches logicielles de pilotage automatique (PX4, ArduPilot ou équivalents).
Interventions opérationnelles & Essais en vol : Participer aux bancs d'essais, campagnes de vol et recettes techniques sur site client.

(Déplacements ponctuels et ciblés : 5 à 6 missions courtes par an, à l’international).

Pont avec la R&D & Qualification : Élaborer et piloter les campagnes d'évaluation de nos nouvelles centrales face à des scénarios sévères (brouillage/leurrage GNSS, environnements contestés) et exprimer les besoins d'évolution produit.
Transmission & Mentorat : Servir de point d’escalade technique ultime et accompagner activement la montée en compétences de nos ingénieurs support Niveau 2.

Le profil recherché

Vous Êtes Un Passionné De Robotique Aérienne Et De Navigation, Aimant Allier L'exigence De La Modélisation à La Réalité Du Vol

Formation & Expérience : Diplôme d’ingénieur (Bac+5) en systèmes embarqués, robotique, mécatronique ou automatique, avec une dizaine d’années d’expérience sur un poste similaire (ingénierie d'application, intégration systèmes de drones, navigation/guidage).
Cadre réglementaire : Poste soumis à une procédure d'habilitation Défense nationale.

Expertise Indispensable

Maîtrise des technologies de positionnement et d'orientation : GNSS et navigation inertielle (IMU / INS).
Expérience avérée dans l’écosystème des drones militaires / UAV tactiques.
Pratique opérationnelle des autopilotes open-source ou industriels (PX4, ArduPilot).
Outils d'analyse de données et traitement de mesures (Python ou Matlab).

Atouts Différentiateurs (très Appréciés)

Notions solides en navigation à l'estime (Dead Reckoning en environnement GNSS dégradé/brouillé).
Connaissance des capteurs de perception complémentaire (LiDAR, vision, SLAM).
Langues : Anglais courant impératif (échanges internationaux quotidiens).

Flexibilité d'organisation et télétravail ponctuel possible (l'activité restant ancrée sur site au contact du matériel, des bancs de test et de l'équipe).

Titres-restaurant, CSE actif, afterworks réguliers et deux séminaires d'entreprise par an.

jobs.title: Environmental Impact Assessment Graduate - Dublin - Start between Nov 26 - Jan 27
jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our

services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of nearly 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

Our Impact Assessment Practice team are currently recruiting a graduate within our Dublin office to start between Nov 26 - Jan 27.

About our Team

Impact Assessment is part of the Environment business, which comprises around 730 professionals across the UK and Republic of Ireland. The team delivers environment and sustainability solutions to both public and private sector clients and plays a leading role in addressing the climate and biodiversity emergencies.

It comprises the following practice areas: Acoustics; Air Quality; Ecology; Geospatial & Data Services; Heritage; Landscape; Water Environment; Impact Assessment; Planning; Climate Change, Sustainability & Resilience; Stakeholder Engagement; and ESIA & ESDD (international environment and sustainability work). Our IAPA work includes:
Coordinating multidisciplinary environmental inputs across a wide range of infrastructure development projects, helping them to gain development consent
Working with clients and design teams to identify environmental constraints, avoid impacts and develop solutions, as well as delivering benefits where possible
Coordinating the preparation of environmental assessment reports
Post-planning consent support to projects (including during project construction and operation)

Projects

AECOM are at the forefront of delivering Environmental Impact Assessments for the nationally significant infrastructure projects that are providing for our future. Key projects include sustainable energy generation and transmission and water distribution.

Here's what you'll do:

We need people with inquiring minds who can ask the questions to understand and then shape projects to achieve environmentally beneficial outcomes. The ability to work with people with different perspectives is essential to understand what Clients really need, what the design means and how it matters to stakeholders. So, communication – verbal and written – to interact with others and seek understanding, is important, but we accept that it is a skill that develops over time. We like people with an appetite to learn and develop – taking personal responsibility, but understanding how to confirm that we are getting to a good outcome.

Enjoy the Perks

At AECOM, you'll enjoy a range of core and personalised benefits designed to support your future and well-being, customised to fit your lifestyle. Take advantage of career development opportunities, our flexible hybrid working model to ensure a work-life balance that suits your lifestyle, technical practice networks, AECOM University, and volunteering days.

Here is what you will get from us!

On the job support and learning

When a graduate starts at AECOM, we pair them with a senior member of the team who will guide and mentor them through their initial period working on live projects and business development tasks, to support with any technical queries.

Graduate Development Programme

Our 2 year graduate ADVANCE programme is designed to help you build your career in AECOM. You will attend a number of instructor-led training sessions where you will meet and hear from people across the business and take part in a series of interactive activities to equip you with the knowledge and skills you need to succeed in your role. Alongside the instructor-led elements of the ADVANCE programme, you will also engage with an online curriculum via AECOM University and have the opportunity to join the ADVANCE webinar series. We will provide you with all the support and tools you need to achieve your professional development ambitions, which may include Chartership with the relevant international professional institution eg Institute for Sustainability and Environmental Professionals (ISEP), Institute of Environmental Science (IES).

We have more than 750 graduates on our programmes across the UK and Ireland from more than 40 different disciplines, each making a tangible difference to the environment in which we live and work.

See our digital early careers e-brochure here

Qualifications

Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?

Here’s what we’re looking for:

Ideally, you will have a relevant first degree and, potentially, a relevant post-graduate degree.

Relevant first or post-graduate degree subjects include: environmental impact assessment,
environmental economics, environmental management, environmental planning, environmental policy, environmental science, geography, housing (sustainable, planning, regeneration and urban management), social science, sustainable development.
A good understanding of the potential for digital solutions to assist in tackling environment and sustainability challenges and be able to help us in delivering our digital transformation agenda
Willingness and ability to travel is essential. A full driving licence or access to reliable transport would be beneficial as the role will involve travel for site surveys and possible transportation of site equipment
Ability to work flexibly under pressure, responding to changing project and programme demands
Good communications skills – verbal and written (fluent in English) – with the confidence to engage with a variety of people (clients, colleagues, stakeholders and sub-contractors alike) and the aptitude to rationally explain, explore and discuss technical issues and capture feedback
Ability to work as a team
Time Management - Work within schedules to coordinate the completion of tasks through to final project completion
Willingness and ability to learn
Strong research and report writing skills (including web-based research) to support team on technical issues influencing project development
Ability to summarise technical information effectively and demonstrate diligent research techniques
Strong skills in Microsoft Office specifically Word, Excel, PowerPoint
Strong numerate skills
Self-starter and enthusiastic, develops and delivers work under own initiative.
Solid attention to detail and thorough approach to work
Strong organisational skills
Commercial awareness for business development, marketing, and proposal preparation.

We celebrate diversity, including neurodiversity, and believe it enriches our team. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and abilities. If you are an applicant with a disability that requires reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us at ReasonableAccommodations@aecom.com

At AECOM, we value everyone's unique contributions and perspectives. If you meet some of the requirements above or have transferable skills you believe would benefit us, we would be delighted to hear from you!

Additional Information

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible since CVs will be reviewed, and candidates selected for an advanced offer start.

Please include a covering letter with your application and provide all predicted and/or obtained academic grades.

You must have permanent right to work in the Republic of Ireland as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.

Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity

You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.

You will help us foster a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.

AECOM provides a wide array of compensation, benefits and well-being programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.

Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

We are a Disability Confident Employer and will offer an interview to applicants who have a disability or long-term condition, who meet the minimum/essential criteria for the role. Please let us know using this email address ReasonableAccommodationsUKI@aecom.com if you would like to apply through the Disability Confident Interview Scheme.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Environmental Field Technician
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Project Manager
plans, coordinates, and oversees safe, efficient environmental field work in accordance with Field Work Orders (FWOs), company procedures, client expectations, and regulatory requirements. This role connects Project Management, Field Operations, clients, vendors, contractors, and field personnel; ensures work is properly scheduled, staffed, equipped, documented, and completed; and provides field leadership and support as needed.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Report writing
Lead tasks on more complex projects
Client interaction
Regulatory interaction
Troubleshooting
Budgeting/costing projects
Participate in field activities
Prepare FWOs, schedules, drawings, permits, sampling requirements, site information, and other project documents before field work begins.
Schedule and coordinate qualified personnel, vehicles, equipment, materials, lodging, and vendors;
Perform or lead environmental sampling, monitoring, investigation, remediation, well installation, and related field services in accordance with project and regulatory requirements.
Direct employees, temporary staff, and contractors; assign work, provide training and coaching, monitor performance, and reinforce accountability and professionalism.
Maintain a safety-first work environment, verify required training and PPE, report incidents and unsafe conditions, and stop or delay work when necessary.
Coordinate waste pickups and disposal; prepare, track, and retain manifests and supporting records through final disposition.
Ensure timely submission of FWOs, field notes, sampling records, photographs, manifests, and other required documentation.
Communicate project status, field conditions, deviations, equipment or personnel concerns, and recommended solutions to appropriate stakeholders.

ACCOUNTABILITY & PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Success is measured by safe, well-planned, adequately staffed and equipped field work that meets project requirements, is documented promptly, and is completed with minimal avoidable delays. The role is expected to anticipate needs, resolve issues, maintain an accurate field calendar, and keep project progressing.

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

Required

High school diploma or GED and relevant environmental, construction, industrial, or field-services experience.
Valid driver’s license
Ability to develop and/or execute FWOs, collect and document field information accurately, and communicate effectively with employees, contractors, clients, and Project Managers.
Ability to work outdoors, operate or learn field equipment safely, manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and work independently or as part of a team.

Preferred

Associate or bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, construction management, project management, or a related field.
40hr HAZWOPER certification;
OCC Environmental Consultant, AST/UST Remover
ASB/LBP Licenses
Experience with environmental sampling or remediation, field equipment, waste manifests, project coordination, and leading crews or contractors.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

Project coordination, scheduling, organization, prioritization, and problem solving.
Clear written and verbal communication with employees, clients, vendors, contractors, and regulators.
Leadership, coaching, accountability, and collaborative decision-making.
Environmental sampling, field documentation, basic equipment troubleshooting, and recognition of unusual or unsafe conditions.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn OES scheduling, project-management, documentation, and communication systems.

WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Work outdoors in varying weather and at construction, industrial, and environmental project sites, including uneven terrain.
Stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb, and lift, carry, push, or pull equipment and materials consistent with job requirements.
Wear required PPE and work around vehicles, machinery, heavy equipment, and environmental sampling equipment.
Travel between offices, project sites, client locations, vendors, and disposal facilities; overnight, extended hours, or weekend work may be required.

Reasonable accommodation may be made for qualified individuals with disabilities consistent with applicable law.

CORE OES COMPETENCIES

• Safety

• Integrity

• Accountability

• Teamwork

• Communication

• Professionalism

• Organization

• Quality

• Reliability & Customer Service

• Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Protect confidential company, employee, client, and project information.
Participate in required meetings, training, and continuous-improvement activities.
Perform other duties as assigned based on business needs.

The Project is to be constructed on a parcel of land located along State Highway 87 south of Port Arthur, Texas, between the inner coastal waterway bridge and Keith Lake. The Infrastructure Global Business Unit (GBU) is executing site civil and marine scopes of work associated with our scopes of work on the Energy GBU LNG projects. As the #1 LNG EPC contractor by installed capacity, Bechtel has the capability to successfully deliver a broad range of LNG projects through our integrated EPC self-perform model, strategic partnerships, and proven experience in LNG project delivery. Job Description

General Functions:

The Environmental Programs Administrator is responsible for supervising two or more environmental programs or teams and for developing performance goals aligned with the Planning, Environmental and Development Services (PEDS) Strategic Management Plan coordinating work priorities, and ensuring effective delivery of environmental services. Work is performed under the general supervision of the EPD Division Manager and Assistant Manager. Incumbent must be able to exercise independent judgment in the oversight and supervision of assigned responsibilities.

Representative Duties/Assignments:

Advises EPD Division leadership and, as appropriate, senior County management, the Board of County Commissioners, and the Environmental Protection Commission or other County Advisory Boards on environmental, regulatory, permitting, compliance, and policy matters.
Coordinates the preparation of Board agenda items, public hearing materials, briefings, reports, correspondence, and other technical or executive-level work products.
Represents EPD in interactions with citizens, applicants, consultants, regulated entities, public interest groups, County departments, municipalities, and local, state, and federal regulatory agencies.
Provides leadership, direction, and oversight for assigned environmental programs, teams, regulatory functions, and special initiatives.
Supervises environmental professionals and/or program supervisors; establishes expectations, develops staff, supports hiring and succession planning, and promotes accountability for results.
Monitors, analyzes, and facilitates operations and activities associated with environmental permitting, compliance & enforcement, development review, pollution prevention, water-quality, and stormwater-related programs, waste-management permitting, natural resources management, and other environmental functions as assigned.
Provides direction on complex or sensitive environmental permitting, compliance, enforcement, development, and regulatory matters and assists with resolution of internal and external concerns or complaints.
Supports the development, interpretation, implementation, and update of environmental codes, ordinances, policies, procedures, and program requirements.
Assists with development and monitoring of budgets, contracts, grants, performance goals, workload measures, and other resources necessary for effective program delivery.
Directs or participates in studies, surveys, technical evaluations, and specialized research related to environmental matters.
Promotes consistent application of County, Department, and Division objectives, policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements while maintaining a high level of public service.
May serve in a higher-level leadership capacity during the absence of Division management.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's degree in environmental or civil engineering, environmental law or natural sciences or a related field, and seven years of environmental protection experience, to include three years in a supervisory role. An equivalent combination of relevant education or experience may be substituted on a year for year basis.

Preferences:

Preference may be given to candidates whose experience demonstrates a combination of environmental program management, regulatory oversight, public/stakeholder engagement, leadership, and technical expertise relevant to EPD operations.

Desired experience may include:

Public Relations, communication, GIS, technical analysis, environmental field methods, or other specialized environmental tools and practices applicable to assigned responsibilities.

Tuition reimbursement program.

Essential Job Duties

The
Sheth plant evolutionary ecology lab
in the
Department of Plant and Microbial Biology
at
North Carolina State University
(Raleigh, NC) is currently seeking field technician to participate in an NSF -funded study (
https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2220928&HistoricalAwards=false
) under the direction of Dr. Seema Sheth and in collaboration with Drs. Susana Wadgymar (Davidson College), Jill Anderson (University of Georgia), Megan DeMarche (University of Georgia), and Emily Josephs (Michigan State University).

The project combines approaches from evolutionary biology, field ecology, and population genomics in a broadly distributed native plant species (
Chamaecrista fasciculata
, Fabaceae) to forecast population dynamics range-wide under climate change. The technician will be part of a dynamic, dedicated, and engaged research group as well as a member of a multidisciplinary and multi-institution collaborative group that includes Botanic Garden and conservation professionals.

The successful candidate will contribute to a collaborative study of eco-evolutionary responses to climate in the partridge pea,
Chamaecrista fasciculata
, an annual legume that grows in disturbed habitats in central and eastern North America. The technician’s primary responsibilities involve collaborating with the PIs and other researchers to establish and maintain a large common garden experiment and to collect data from ~6,000 transplanted seeds at Mason Farm Biological Reserve in Chapel Hill, NC. This work includes preparing seeds for planting, planting seeds, setting up the garden infrastructure, building open-top chambers, collecting data on traits and fitness, entering data, maintenance tasks in the garden (e.g., weeding), processing samples in the lab, and communicating with Dr. Sheth and other team members. The technician will also have opportunities to train and mentor undergraduate students and work with graduate students.

Extraordinary Teams Building Inspiring Projects

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments. They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report.

Project Overview

The Cheniere Sabine Pass Liquefaction (SPL) Project is a Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) export facility located along the Sabine River estuary on the southeastern coast of Cameron Parish, Louisiana. Bulk early work for Stage 1 began at the 1,000+ acre facility in August 2012 and by December 2022, Bechtel had successfully and safely turned over the final phase of Stage 4 to Cheniere. The SPL campus now consists of six operating Trains with an LNG production capacity of approximately 27 million tons per year (MTPA), 3 Jetty superstructures that can accommodate the world’s largest vessels, and dozens of associated buildings and utilities.

Sabine Pass Liquefaction Stage 5 Expansion Project (SPL5) is the newest phase at the SPL facility. It will consist of one liquefaction process train with a production capacity of approximately 5 MTPA; one boil-off gas reliquefaction unit; tie-ins to existing storage tanks, ship-loading facilities, and flare systems; and associated utility support infrastructure. SPL5 will perform this work predominantly on a direct hire basis with support from only a few specialty and service subcontractors.

Job Summary

The Project Environmental Manager is the primary contact for environmental permits, planning, performance, and compliance. This includes technical support and guidance on regulatory requirements and field activities to mitigate risk or harm to environmentally sensitive areas, resources, and communities. The position includes communication, training, interface with regulatory agencies, and data and document management. The overarching responsibility is the development and implementation of an environmental management and compliance program for a large-scale project.

Major Responsibilities

Supervises the Project’s environmental program, in compliance with Bechtel’s ESH Management System, and contract and regulatory requirements.
Ensures that environmental requirements are integrated in planning documents, design criteria, work plans, schedules, training programs, and subcontract documents. Communicates with internal and external stakeholders on environmental requirements and actions, inclusive of project personnel, subcontractors, and regulatory agencies. Emphasizes and uses risk assessment, data analysis, and Bechtel’s ESH Management System to aid environmental performance, corrective actions, and technical guidance.
Participates in ESH emergency preparedness planning, and investigates and helps resolve environmental incidents.
Prepares and maintains required documentation and conducts inspections, monitoring, and sampling to assess site conditions and compliance with contractual commitments, laws and regulations, environmental permits, and Bechtel requirements.
Delivers training and awareness campaigns on environmental, sustainability, and regulatory compliance to the project’s workforce through various forums. Supervises and guides assigned environmental personnel, and participates in safety and health components of the ESH program.

Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) related to environmental sciences, field biology, or natural resources and 8 -10 years of relevant experience or 12-14 years of relevant work experience

Required Knowledge And Skills

Prior experience with environmental regulatory requirements, impact assessment, and mitigation practices for large-scale projects. Technical skills, work experience, and knowledge of various environmental sciences applicable to the engineering and construction industry.
Knowledge and experience with ISO 14001 Management System standards. Knowledge and experience with environmental mitigation practices (e.g., habitat protection, waste management, stormwater and erosion control, cultural resources).
Knowledge and experience in environmental permitting and regulatory approvals.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including technical writing and data management.
Able to traverse and work outdoors under various weather and site conditions. Experience managing environmental subcontractors or consultants.
This position has a work scope that includes field inspections and the physical ability to conduct field inspections which require the following activities: extensive walking in and around a construction site, climbing ladders, climbing scaffolding, working on elevated platforms, working on uneven surfaces, and working in small or confined spaces.
Some lifting may be required. Must have the ability to walk into and out of the project (enter/egress).
Must be able to use appropriate standard issued Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) required for each assigned task (i.e., harness, life vest, lift buckets, etc.)

Total Rewards/Benefits

For decades, Bechtel has worked to inspire the next generation of employees and beyond! Because our teams face some of the world's toughest challenges, we offer robust benefits to ensure our people thrive. Whether it is advancing careers, delivering programs to enhance our culture, or providing time to recharge, Bechtel has the benefits to build a legacy of sustainable growth.
